reference: GNU binutils ar from the runner's read-only /usr tree, compared against the candidate with the same deterministic private fixture script. Bash type/help checks use the builtin metadata contract. Non-parity archive contracts assert the documented 8-byte magic, 60-byte fixed-width header, deterministic metadata and retained member bytes independently of GNU output.
coverage: Bash builtin registration and documented help metadata
Deterministic archive creation, member listing, and archive bytes
GNU behavior for a requested symbol index with no ELF symbols
Quick append including duplicate member names
GNU replace behavior for retaining non-replaced members
GNU long-name table creation, listing, and selected extraction
Selected and full extraction, including odd/even member bodies
Valid empty archive and missing archive errors
Independent archive format and retained metadata contract
Non-deterministic -U source metadata using ordinary fixed timestamps and mode
Independent existing local archive symlink and hardlink contract
Independent short spaced-name retention and replacement contracts
Independent overlong imported-name refusal without archive changes
exclusions: Full ELF/linker compatibility, thin/BSD archives, positioning/update modifiers, devices, hostile paths and privileged operations are outside this suite.
Actual ownership changes and exhaustive metadata combinations are excluded; -U writes use naturally identical runner ownership and ordinary fixed touch/chmod fixtures.

cases.purpose: The ar command is registered as a Bash builtin and remains available with the candidate's empty PATH.
cases.script: type -t ar

cases.purpose: Bash help exposes the documented operation synopsis and deterministic-write description for ar.
cases.script:
doc=$(help ar)
[[ $doc == *"Create, list, or extract simple ar archives."* ]]
[[ $doc == *"Writes are deterministic"* ]]
[[ $doc == *"ar [-D|-U] -t|-x|-r|-q|-s|s ARCHIVE [FILE...]"* ]]
printf 'help metadata present\n'

cases.purpose: Create a deterministic archive from two small files without requesting a symbol index, list its members in order, and compare archive bytes and fixture modes with GNU ar.
cases.script:
printf 'alpha payload\n' > alpha.txt
printf 'beta data\n' > beta.dat
ar rc library.a alpha.txt beta.dat
ar t library.a

cases.purpose: Request a symbol index for a text-only archive; compare the serialized archive, which must contain no empty symbol-table record.
cases.script:
printf 'plain data\n' > payload.txt
ar rcs library.a payload.txt
ar t library.a

cases.purpose: GNU ar q appends rather than replacing a same-named member; compare duplicate listing order and resulting archive bytes.
cases.script:
printf 'first version\n' > item.txt
ar qc library.a item.txt
printf 'second version\n' > item.txt
ar q library.a item.txt
ar t library.a

cases.purpose: Replace a matching member, retain unrelated members in order, and append new members; compare listing and archive bytes with GNU ar.
cases.script:
printf 'old first\n' > first.txt
printf 'keep this member\n' > keep.txt
ar rc library.a first.txt keep.txt
printf 'new first\n' > first.txt
printf 'new member\n' > added.txt
ar r library.a first.txt added.txt
ar t library.a

cases.purpose: Create an archive with a basename longer than the 15-byte ar header field, list it, then extract just that member over a changed source file. Compare the GNU long-name table, archive bytes, and restored content.
cases.script:
member=this_is_a_long_member_name.txt
printf 'archived long-name data\n' > "$member"
ar rc library.a "$member"
printf 'changed local data\n' > "$member"
ar x library.a "$member"
IFS= read -r restored < "$member"
printf '%s\n' "$restored"

cases.purpose: Extract one requested member over an existing file, and verify that the unselected member is left untouched.
cases.script:
printf 'archive-one\n' > one.txt
printf 'archive-two\n' > two.txt
ar rc library.a one.txt two.txt
printf 'local-one\n' > one.txt
printf 'local-two\n' > two.txt
ar x library.a one.txt
IFS= read -r one < one.txt
IFS= read -r two < two.txt
printf '%s|%s\n' "$one" "$two"

cases.purpose: Extract all members whose bodies have odd and even lengths, checking ar record padding and exact extracted bytes against GNU ar.
cases.script:
printf 'abc' > odd.bin
printf 'wxyz' > even.bin
ar rc library.a odd.bin even.bin
printf 'xxx' > odd.bin
printf 'yyyy' > even.bin
ar x library.a
read -r -N 3 odd < odd.bin
read -r -N 4 even < even.bin
printf 'odd=%s even=%s\n' "$odd" "$even"

cases.purpose: The installed reference ar t returns status 9 for a missing relative archive; no fixture file is created.
cases.script: ar t missing.a

cases.purpose: List and index a valid archive with no members; indexing must leave it empty.
cases.script:
printf '!<arch>\n' > empty.a
ar t empty.a
ar s empty.a
ar t empty.a

cases.purpose: Refreshing an index repeatedly for ordinary data emits no artificial member.
cases.script:
printf 'payload\n' > plain
ar rc library.a plain
ar s library.a
ar s library.a
ar t library.a

cases.purpose: Retain an unrelated long name and replace another long name while appending a new member; compare the rebuilt GNU name table and extracted contents.
cases.script:
printf 'old\n' > replace_long_member.txt
printf 'keep\n' > retained_long_member.txt
ar rc library.a replace_long_member.txt retained_long_member.txt
printf 'new\n' > replace_long_member.txt
printf 'added\n' > add.txt
ar rcs library.a replace_long_member.txt add.txt
ar t library.a
ar x library.a

cases.purpose: Replacing a new basename retains all existing members and appends it.
cases.script:
printf 'one\n' > one
printf 'two\n' > two
ar rc library.a one
ar r library.a two
ar t library.a

cases.purpose: An unavailable replacement input fails without destroying the original valid archive.
cases.script:
printf 'keep\n' > one
ar rc library.a one
status=0
ar r library.a missing || status=$?
printf 'status=%d\n' "$status"
ar t library.a

cases.purpose: Extracting from a missing relative archive reports the installed reference status.
cases.script: ar x missing.a

cases.purpose: Indexing a missing relative archive reports the installed reference status.
cases.script: ar s missing.a

cases.purpose: Independently check fixed-width ar serialization, unchanged uid/gid/mtime/mode for an untouched member, and normalized new metadata using a valid hand-serialized local archive. This is a documented format contract, not GNU byte parity.
cases.script:
printf '!<arch>\n' > library.a
printf '%-16s%-12s%-6s%-6s%-8s%-10s`\n' keep/ 946684800 12 34 751 4 >> library.a
printf 'old\n' >> library.a
printf 'new\n' > fresh
ar r library.a fresh
exec 3< library.a
check_bytes() {
    local got
    IFS= read -r -N "${#1}" got <&3
    [[ $got == "$1" ]]
}
check_bytes $'!<arch>\n'
printf -v header '%-16s%-12s%-6s%-6s%-8s%-10s`\n' keep/ 946684800 12 34 751 4
check_bytes "$header"
check_bytes $'old\n'
printf -v header '%-16s%-12s%-6s%-6s%-8s%-10s`\n' fresh/ 0 0 0 644 4
check_bytes "$header"
check_bytes $'new\n'
if IFS= read -r -N 1 extra <&3; then exit 1; fi
exec 3<&-
printf 'fixed archive layout and retained metadata verified\n'
cases.stdout: fixed archive layout and retained metadata verified

cases.purpose: Replacement changes the first matching duplicate while retaining later duplicate contents and all other members.
cases.script:
printf 'first\n' > item
printf 'keep\n' > other
ar qc library.a item other
printf 'second\n' > item
ar q library.a item
printf 'third\n' > item
ar r library.a item
ar t library.a

cases.purpose: Ordinary -U index refresh of an archive containing data and no symbols does not insert a fake member or change existing metadata.
cases.script:
printf '!<arch>\n' > library.a
printf '%-16s%-12s%-6s%-6s%-8s%-10s`\n' keep/ 946684800 12 34 751 4 >> library.a
printf 'old\n' >> library.a
ar -U s library.a
ar t library.a

cases.purpose: Seed ordinary private source timestamps and mode with touch/chmod, then compare -U archive metadata and payload bytes. No account change or privileged environment is needed. Cover both replacement and quick-append writers.
cases.script:
printf 'fixed metadata\n' > item
touch -t 200001010000.00 item
chmod 751 item
ar -U rc library.a item
ar t library.a
ar -U qc appended.a item
ar t appended.a

cases.purpose: A non-directory intermediate component is an ordinary missing archive path; verify its status against the installed reference.
cases.script:
printf 'ordinary file\n' > parent
ar t parent/missing.a

cases.purpose: Preserve existing local archive link behavior: replacement follows a private symlink and keeps hard links to the same archive inode. Assert the original repository contract independently.
cases.script:
printf 'old\n' > item
ar rc real.a item
ln real.a hard.a
ln -s real.a sym.a
printf 'new\n' > item
ar r sym.a item
[[ -L sym.a && real.a -ef hard.a ]]
printf 'local\n' > item
ar x hard.a
IFS= read -r value < item
[[ $value == new ]]
printf 'local archive links preserved\n'

cases.purpose: Append an unrelated member to a small hand-serialized archive and independently verify that a short spaced name, metadata and body remain exact under the existing slash-terminated encoding convention.
cases.script:
printf '!<arch>\n' > library.a
printf '%-16s%-12s%-6s%-6s%-8s%-10s`\n' 'two words/' 946684800 12 34 751 4 >> library.a
printf 'old\n' >> library.a
printf 'new\n' > fresh
ar r library.a fresh
exec 3< library.a
check_bytes() {
    local got
    IFS= read -r -N "${#1}" got <&3
    [[ $got == "$1" ]]
}
check_bytes $'!<arch>\n'
printf -v header '%-16s%-12s%-6s%-6s%-8s%-10s`\n' 'two words/' 946684800 12 34 751 4
check_bytes "$header"
check_bytes $'old\n'
printf -v header '%-16s%-12s%-6s%-6s%-8s%-10s`\n' fresh/ 0 0 0 644 4
check_bytes "$header"
check_bytes $'new\n'
if IFS= read -r -N 1 extra <&3; then exit 1; fi
exec 3<&-
printf 'short spaced name retained exactly\n'

cases.purpose: Replace a short spaced basename in a small hand-serialized archive; independently assert replacement in place, deterministic new metadata, retained following member and exact EOF so an extra appended duplicate cannot pass.
cases.script:
printf '!<arch>\n' > library.a
printf '%-16s%-12s%-6s%-6s%-8s%-10s`\n' 'two words/' 946684800 12 34 751 4 >> library.a
printf 'old\n' >> library.a
printf '%-16s%-12s%-6s%-6s%-8s%-10s`\n' keep/ 946684800 12 34 751 4 >> library.a
printf 'stay' >> library.a
printf 'new\n' > 'two words'
ar r library.a 'two words'
exec 3< library.a
check_bytes() {
    local got
    IFS= read -r -N "${#1}" got <&3
    [[ $got == "$1" ]]
}
check_bytes $'!<arch>\n'
printf -v header '%-16s%-12s%-6s%-6s%-8s%-10s`\n' 'two words/' 0 0 0 644 4
check_bytes "$header"
check_bytes $'new\n'
printf -v header '%-16s%-12s%-6s%-6s%-8s%-10s`\n' keep/ 946684800 12 34 751 4
check_bytes "$header"
check_bytes stay
if IFS= read -r -N 1 extra <&3; then exit 1; fi
exec 3<&-
printf 'short spaced name replaced exactly once\n'
cases.stdout: short spaced name replaced exactly once

cases.purpose: A benign valid GNU name-table entry with a 256-byte imported name exceeds the builtin's name buffer. Replacing an unrelated file must fail before writing and leave every original archive byte unchanged.
cases.script:
printf -v long_name '%0256d' 0
long_name=${long_name//0/n}
printf -v table '%s/\n' "$long_name"
printf -v table_header '%-16s%-12s%-6s%-6s%-8s%-10s`\n' // '' '' '' '' "${#table}"
printf -v member_header '%-16s%-12s%-6s%-6s%-8s%-10s`\n' /0 946684800 12 34 751 4
original=$'!<arch>\n'"$table_header$table$member_header"$'old\n'
printf '%s' "$original" > library.a
printf 'new\n' > fresh
status=0
ar r library.a fresh || status=$?
[[ $status -eq 1 ]]
exec 3< library.a
IFS= read -r -N "${#original}" actual <&3
[[ $actual == "$original" ]]
if IFS= read -r -N 1 extra <&3; then exit 1; fi
exec 3<&-
printf 'overlong imported name refused without changes\n'
cases.stdout: overlong imported name refused without changes

cases.purpose: A valid ar magic followed by a truncated member header is rejected by both implementations with a nonzero status and diagnostic.
cases.script:
printf '!<arch>\nX' > partial.a
ar t partial.a
